function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Develop a comprehensive, source-grounded reconstruction of the Internet Research Agency's 2016 social-media influence operation using only evidence available from benchmark tools. Collect and cite the exact source identifiers returned by the research system for every substantive assertion. Cover: (1) facts alleged in relevant United States Department of Justice indictments, clearly labeled as allegations unless independently established; (2) findings, judgments, and confidence assessments in United States Senate investigative materials; (3) platform-provided data and disclosures from companies such as Facebook, Twitter, Google, and Reddit where available; (4) identified or alleged online personas, accounts, pages, groups, organizations, and operators, without inventing identities or treating uncertain attribution as fact; (5) funding sources, payment mechanisms, shell or front organizations, and organizational relationships; and (6) stated or inferred objectives, tactics, target audiences, timeline, geographic or demographic targeting, and outcomes. Build an evidence matrix that distinguishes documented fact, allegation, assessment, inference, and unresolved uncertainty. Identify corroboration across independent sources, gaps, contradictions, disputed attribution, and differences in scope or methodology. Do not rely on unsupported relationship names or IDs. Return enough detail for a final report with a readable chronological and relational narrative, plus structured data: findings with question, answer, supporting_entities, and source_references; claims with claim and source_references; reasoning_steps with id, conclusion, premise_entities, and premise_relations; contradictions with contradiction_id, description, and source_references. Every source reference must be a source ID actually returned by the benchmark tools."}
function.name: ConductResearch
